name: Andersen Corporation
desc: Family-owned maker of wood and composite windows and patio doors, including the Renewal by Andersen replacement business.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States and Canada through dealers and retailers; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: Mainly North American home-improvement brand; Miami, Austin and Las Vegas races could support consumer marketing, but fit is modest.

name: SMS group GmbH
desc: Family-owned German engineering group that designs and builds plants and machinery for the steel and non-ferrous metals industry.
markets: Supplies steel and metals producers worldwide, with subsidiaries across Europe, the Americas, China, India and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B engineering firm; F1 hospitality could reach steel-industry customers in Gulf and Asian race markets, but brand marketing is limited.

name: Hoogwegt Groep B.V.
desc: Family-owned Dutch trading company that buys and sells dairy ingredients such as milk powders, butter and cheese.
markets: Trades dairy ingredients between producers and buyers in many countries across Europe, Asia, the Americas and Africa.
rationale: Low-profile B2B commodity trader with little consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond limited client hospitality.

name: Linfox Pty Ltd
desc: Fox family-owned logistics company providing road transport, warehousing and supply-chain services, plus Armaguard cash logistics.
markets: Operates in Australia and New Zealand and in several South-East Asian countries including Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia.
rationale: Logistics brand with Australian and South-East Asian reach; Melbourne and Singapore races offer B2B hospitality, a plausible but secondary fit.

name: Boparan Holdco Ltd (2 Sisters Food Group)
desc: Holding company of 2 Sisters Food Group, a British poultry processor and food manufacturer supplying supermarkets.
markets: Supplies UK retailers and food-service customers, with some operations elsewhere in Europe; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: Own-label supplier to supermarkets with little consumer brand marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Great Lakes Cheese Company, Inc.
desc: Family- and employee-owned US company that makes, cuts and packages natural and processed cheese for retailers and food service.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Largely private-label US dairy supplier with no consumer brand to promote; weak F1 fit.

name: Alfred Kärcher SE & Co. KG
desc: Family-owned German maker of pressure washers, floor cleaners, vacuums and professional cleaning equipment for homes and businesses.
markets: Sells in most countries worldwide through subsidiaries in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global consumer and professional brand with strong marketing culture; F1 offers worldwide visibility and a German engineering showcase.

name: Gruppo PAM
desc: Family-owned Italian supermarket group operating PAM, Panorama and In's Mercato grocery stores.
markets: Stores in Italy only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic grocer; only Italian races at Monza and Imola could help, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Publix Super Markets, Inc.
desc: Employee-owned US supermarket chain operating grocery stores and pharmacies across Florida and the south-eastern United States.
markets: Stores in Florida and other south-eastern US states only; expansion limited to the US Southeast.
rationale: Regional US grocer; the Miami Grand Prix gives a local hook, but national and global F1 reach is wasted.

name: Carahsoft Technology Corp.
desc: Privately held IT distributor that resells software, cloud and cybersecurity products to US government agencies through reseller partners.
markets: Customers are mainly US federal, state and local government bodies and education; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Government-focused reseller with little brand marketing; weak F1 fit, though vendor partners sponsor F1.

name: Kingston Technology Corporation
desc: Privately held US maker of computer memory modules, solid-state drives, USB flash drives and memory cards.
markets: Sells worldwide with offices and manufacturing in the United States, Taiwan, China and Europe.
rationale: Global tech hardware brand selling to gamers and PC builders; F1 offers a technology showcase and worldwide consumer reach.
changed: Sold its HyperX gaming peripherals brand to HP in 2021

name: HITT Contracting Inc.
desc: US general contractor building offices, data centres, healthcare and other commercial facilities.
markets: Works in the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B contractor with little need for global brand exposure; weak F1 fit.

name: Sundt Construction, Inc.
desc: Employee-owned US contractor building transportation, industrial, healthcare, education and commercial projects.
markets: Works mainly in the western and southern United States; no verified international activity.
rationale: Domestic contractor with no consumer brand and US-only clients; F1's global exposure offers little value, so a weak fit.

name: K-VA-T Food Stores, Inc.
desc: Employee-owned operator of the Food City supermarket chain in Virginia, Tennessee and Kentucky.
markets: Stores in the Appalachian region of the United States only; no international plans.
rationale: Regional US grocer with no nearby Grand Prix and no need for global reach; weak F1 fit.

name: ABC Supply Co., Inc.
desc: Privately held US wholesale distributor of roofing, siding, windows and other exterior building products to contractors.
markets: Branches across the United States; no verified international expansion. Long-time IndyCar sponsor.
rationale: Has motorsport marketing experience through IndyCar, but customers are US contractors; plausible only around US races.

name: Sazerac Company
desc: Family-owned US spirits company owning brands such as Buffalo Trace, Fireball, Southern Comfort and Blanton's.
markets: Largest sales in the United States; brands are exported to Europe, Asia-Pacific and other markets.
rationale: Premium bourbon and whisky brands suit F1 hospitality and global premium marketing; rival spirits brands already sponsor F1.

name: Oxbow Corporation
desc: Koch family-owned company that processes, trades and ships petroleum coke, calcined coke, coal and related carbon products.
markets: Trades and ships carbon products to industrial customers worldwide, with offices and plants in several countries.
rationale: Low-profile commodity business selling to industrial customers, with no consumer brand to build; weak F1 fit.

name: Haworth Inc.
desc: Family-owned US maker of office furniture and workspace interiors, also owning Italian design brands Poltrona Frau and Cassina.
markets: Sells in many countries through dealers and showrooms in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Premium Italian design brands could use F1 hospitality and luxury positioning; plausible but not obvious.

name: Republic National Distributing Company
desc: Privately held US wholesale distributor of wine and spirits to retailers, bars and restaurants.
markets: Distributes in a number of US states only; no international operations.
rationale: Wholesaler whose supplier brands do the consumer marketing; little reason to buy F1 exposure, so a weak fit.

name: SHI International Corp.
desc: Privately held IT reseller and services provider selling software, hardware and cloud solutions to businesses and public bodies.
markets: Mainly US customers, with offices in Canada, the United Kingdom, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B IT provider that could host enterprise clients at races; vendor partners already sponsor F1, so a plausible but modest fit.

name: Tauber Oil Company
desc: Privately held Houston company that markets and trades petroleum products, petrochemicals, natural gas liquids and carbon black feedstock.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States; scope of export activity not verified.
rationale: Low-profile commodity marketer with no consumer brand and few reasons for global exposure; weak F1 fit.

name: The Michaels Companies, Inc.
desc: Arts-and-crafts retailer operating Michaels stores and online sales of craft, framing and seasonal products.
markets: Stores in the United States and Canada; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: North American consumer retailer with a mostly female craft audience; weak F1 fit.
changed: Taken private by Apollo Global Management funds in 2021; previously listed on Nasdaq

name: Hunt Consolidated, Inc.
desc: Hunt family holding company with interests in oil and gas exploration, LNG, real estate, power and investments.
industry: oil and gas and diversified holdings
markets: Operates mainly in the United States, with oil, gas and LNG interests in Peru and other countries.
rationale: Diversified family energy group with little consumer marketing and a low public profile; weak F1 fit.

name: Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.
desc: Tilman Fertitta-owned group running Landry's restaurants, Golden Nugget casinos and hotels, and other hospitality businesses.
markets: Restaurants, hotels and casinos mainly in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Las Vegas casino and hospitality interests fit F1 entertainment; Las Vegas and Austin races offer a local hook.

name: Mary Kay Inc.
desc: Privately held cosmetics and skincare company selling through independent beauty consultants in direct sales.
markets: Sells in dozens of countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific, including China.
rationale: Global beauty brand, but its audience and direct-selling model do not match F1 well; plausible only for a new audience push.

name: Austin Industries, Inc.
desc: Employee-owned US contractor providing commercial building, civil and industrial construction services.
markets: Works mainly in Texas and other US states; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B contractor in Texas with no consumer brand; F1 exposure would be mostly wasted, a weak fit.

name: Zachry Group
desc: US engineering and construction firm serving refining, chemicals, power and LNG customers with construction and maintenance.
markets: Works for energy and industrial clients in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Industrial B2B contractor with no consumer brand, recently through bankruptcy; weak F1 fit.
changed: Zachry Holdings filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2024

name: Mode Transportation
desc: US transportation and logistics company arranging freight services such as truckload, intermodal and brokerage.
markets: Customers in the United States; no verified international operations. Current ownership not confirmed.
rationale: Domestic freight broker with little brand marketing and US-only customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Vitol Group
desc: Employee-owned energy trading company that trades and ships crude oil, refined products, gas and power worldwide.
markets: Trades worldwide from Geneva, London, Houston and Singapore; owns refining, storage and fuel retail assets.
rationale: B2B trader with little need for brand exposure; F1 hospitality could serve energy clients, but fit is weak.

name: REWE Group
desc: German co-operative retail and tourism group running REWE and Penny supermarkets, Billa stores and DER Touristik travel.
markets: Supermarkets in Germany, Austria and Central and Eastern Europe; travel business sells holidays across Europe.
rationale: Mass-market European grocer and tour operator; F1 could support Penny or travel brands, but fit is plausible rather than obvious.

name: State Farm
desc: Policyholder-owned US mutual insurer selling car, home, life and health insurance plus banking products through agents.
markets: Customers in the United States only; sold its Canadian operations to Desjardins in 2015.
rationale: Huge US advertiser but domestic only; F1's US races give some reach, yet most global exposure is wasted.

name: Hengli Group
desc: Chinese private group producing refined oil, petrochemicals, PTA, polyester fibres and textiles; controls listed Hengli Petrochemical.
markets: Operations mainly in China; extent of export sales not verified.
rationale: Industrial commodity producer with little consumer brand; Chinese Grand Prix hospitality is the only hook, so a weak fit.

name: Pacific Construction Group
desc: Chinese privately owned contractor building roads, bridges, municipal infrastructure and buildings.
markets: Works in China; no verified international operations or plans.
rationale: Domestic Chinese contractor with no consumer brand; Shanghai race hospitality is the only possible hook, a weak fit.

name: E.Leclerc
desc: French retail group of independently owned hypermarkets and supermarkets, also selling fuel, travel, optics and cultural goods.
markets: Mainly France, with stores in Spain, Portugal, Poland and Slovenia.
rationale: Mass-market French grocer; the French market alone limits value, so F1 fit is plausible but weak.

name: Edeka Zentrale
desc: Central organisation of Germany's Edeka co-operative supermarket group, which also owns the Netto Marken-Discount chain.
markets: Stores in Germany only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic grocer with large advertising budget but little use for global reach; weak F1 fit.

name: EY (Ernst & Young)
desc: Global network of member firms providing audit, tax, consulting and strategy and transactions services to businesses.
markets: Member firms in more than 150 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Direct rivals Deloitte and PwC already partner with F1 teams; strong B2B hospitality and technology-consulting showcase.

name: Zhejiang Geely Holding Group
desc: Privately owned Chinese car group behind Geely Auto, Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus, Zeekr and Lynk & Co.
markets: Sells cars across China, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific; expanding its brands internationally.
rationale: Global car brands pushing into Europe and the Middle East; F1 offers brand building and a technology showcase.
changed: Zeekr was taken private and merged into Geely Auto in 2025

name: IKEA
desc: Swedish-founded home furnishings brand selling flat-pack furniture and household goods through stores and online.
markets: Stores in more than 60 markets across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, run mainly by Ingka Group.
rationale: Mass-market global brand; F1 could reach young urban buyers, but IKEA has little motorsport marketing history.

name: Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Company (MassMutual)
desc: Policyholder-owned US mutual company selling life insurance, disability insurance, annuities and retirement products.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States; asset manager Barings serves clients internationally.
rationale: Mostly domestic financial brand; US races and client hospitality are the only clear hooks, so fit is modest.

name: New York Life Insurance Company
desc: Policyholder-owned US mutual company selling life insurance, annuities, long-term care and investment products through agents.
markets: Customers in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic insurer with conservative marketing and only US customers; US races are the only hook, a weak fit.

name: ZF Friedrichshafen AG
desc: German supplier of transmissions, driveline, chassis, steering and safety systems for cars, trucks and industrial machines.
markets: Supplies vehicle makers worldwide, with plants in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific. Mainly owned by the Zeppelin Foundation.
rationale: Automotive technology supplier; F1 offers an engineering showcase and hospitality for car-maker customers.

name: Shandong Weiqiao Pioneering Group
desc: Chinese private group producing cotton textiles and aluminium; controls listed aluminium producer China Hongqiao Group.
markets: Production mainly in China; sources bauxite from Guinea and sells products in export markets.
rationale: Industrial commodity producer with no consumer brand to build; weak F1 fit beyond limited client hospitality.

name: Coop Group
desc: Swiss co-operative running supermarkets, department stores and specialist shops, plus Transgourmet wholesale.
markets: Retail in Switzerland; Transgourmet wholesale operates in Germany, Austria, France, Poland and Romania.
rationale: Mainly Swiss retailer and wholesaler; Switzerland hosts no Grand Prix, so F1 fit is weak.

name: KPMG
desc: Global network of member firms providing audit, tax and advisory services to businesses and public bodies.
markets: Member firms in about 140 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Direct rivals Deloitte and PwC already partner with F1 teams; strong B2B hospitality and advisory showcase.

name: Tsingshan Holding Group
desc: Chinese private group producing stainless steel, nickel and battery materials, with large nickel operations in Indonesia.
markets: Production in China and Indonesia, with projects in other countries; sells to steel and battery makers worldwide.
rationale: Industrial metals producer with no consumer brand; battery-materials link to EVs is indirect, so a weak F1 fit.

name: Jiangsu Shagang Group
desc: Chinese privately owned steelmaker producing rebar, wire rod, plate and other steel products.
markets: Steel production and sales mainly in China; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic commodity steelmaker with no consumer brand; Chinese Grand Prix hospitality is the only hook, a weak fit.

name: Les Mousquetaires
desc: French group of independent retailers running Intermarché, Netto, Bricomarché and other store chains.
markets: Mainly France, with stores in Belgium, Portugal and Poland.
rationale: Mass-market European grocer; limited use for global reach, so F1 fit is weak.

name: USAA
desc: Member-owned US provider of insurance, banking and investment services for military members, veterans and their families.
markets: Members in the United States and US military personnel abroad; no wider expansion plans.
rationale: Membership restricted to the US military community; weak F1 fit beyond US races.

name: Migros Group
desc: Swiss co-operative group running supermarkets, specialist retail, food manufacturing, travel, banking and other services.
markets: Mainly Switzerland, with the Tegut supermarket chain in Germany.
rationale: Mainly Swiss retailer; Switzerland hosts no Grand Prix and Migros has little use for global reach, a weak fit.

name: GuideWell Mutual Holding Corporation
desc: Florida mutual holding company whose main business, Florida Blue, sells health insurance and runs health services.
markets: Customers mainly in Florida and other US states; no international operations.
rationale: Florida health insurer; the Miami Grand Prix is a possible local hook, but fit is weak.

name: Système U
desc: French co-operative of independent retailers operating Hyper U, Super U and U Express grocery stores.
markets: Stores in France, including overseas territories; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Domestic French grocer with no international stores; France currently hosts no Grand Prix, so a weak fit.

name: Hailiang Group
desc: Chinese private group making copper pipes and products, also active in education and environmental businesses.
markets: Production mainly in China, with copper plants in South-East Asia and the United States.
rationale: Industrial copper processor with little consumer brand to promote; weak F1 fit beyond client hospitality.

name: EG Group
desc: Operator of fuel stations, convenience stores and franchised food outlets in the United States, Europe and Australia.
markets: Sites in the United States, continental Europe and Australia; owned by Zuber Issa and TDR Capital.
rationale: Fuel forecourt operator with motoring customers; F1 could support its convenience brands, a plausible but modest fit.
changed: Sold its UK and Ireland business to Asda in 2023

name: Achmea
desc: Dutch insurance group selling health, property, life and pension products under brands including Zilveren Kruis and Centraal Beheer.
markets: Mainly the Netherlands, with smaller operations in Slovakia, Turkey and Australia.
rationale: Mainly Dutch insurer; the Dutch Grand Prix ended in 2026, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance Company
desc: Japanese mutual life insurer selling life, medical and annuity products, also owning US insurer StanCorp Financial.
markets: Mainly Japan, plus StanCorp in the United States and stakes in insurers in Europe and Asia.
rationale: Japanese insurer could use the Japanese Grand Prix, but conservative marketing makes F1 a plausible rather than obvious fit.

name: Dairy Farmers of America
desc: US farmer-owned dairy co-operative that markets members' milk and makes fluid milk, cheese and other dairy products.
markets: Operations and most customers in the United States; some dairy ingredient exports.
rationale: Farmer-owned co-operative supplying commodity dairy, mostly in the US; little use for global F1 exposure, a weak fit.

name: Conad
desc: Italian consortium of retailer co-operatives running Conad supermarkets and hypermarkets, including former Auchan Italy stores.
markets: Stores mainly in Italy; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic grocer; Italian races offer some local value, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Wakefern Food Corporation
desc: US retailer-owned co-operative that supplies and supports ShopRite, Price Rite and other member supermarkets.
markets: Serves member stores in the north-eastern United States only.
rationale: Regional US grocery co-operative supplying member stores in the Northeast; little use for global F1 reach, a weak fit.

name: Unimed
desc: Brazilian network of physician-owned medical co-operatives providing health plans, hospitals and medical services.
markets: Customers in Brazil only; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic health co-operative; the São Paulo Grand Prix offers local visibility, but fit is weak.

name: John Swire & Sons
desc: Swire family group with interests in aviation, Coca-Cola bottling, property, shipping, trading and industrial businesses.
markets: Operations mainly in Hong Kong, mainland China and Asia-Pacific, plus the US and UK; controls listed Swire Pacific, a major Cathay Pacific shareholder.
rationale: Asian property, aviation and drinks interests could use Asian races for hospitality; plausible but not obvious.

name: Covéa
desc: French mutual insurance group selling car, home, health and life insurance through MAAF, MMA and GMF.
markets: Mainly France; owns Bermuda-based reinsurer PartnerRe, which serves clients worldwide.
rationale: Mainly French consumer insurer; F1 fit is plausible only for brand building in France.
changed: Acquired reinsurer PartnerRe from Exor in 2022

name: John Lewis Partnership
desc: Employee-owned British retailer running John Lewis department stores and Waitrose supermarkets, plus online sales.
markets: Stores in the United Kingdom only; limited exports of Waitrose products.
rationale: UK-only retailer; the British Grand Prix gives a local hook, but fit is weak.

name: Andel Group
desc: Danish consumer-owned co-operative supplying electricity, running power grids and fibre broadband, and investing in renewables.
markets: Customers mainly in eastern Denmark; no verified wider international expansion.
rationale: Regulated Danish utility with domestic customers; no Danish Grand Prix and little need for global reach, a weak fit.

name: Coop Italia
desc: Consortium of Italian consumer co-operatives running Coop supermarkets and hypermarkets and the Coop own-label range.
markets: Stores in Italy only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic grocer; Italian races offer some local value, but F1 fit is weak.

name: World Wide Technology
desc: Privately held IT solutions provider supplying networking, cloud, security and data-centre technology and services to enterprises.
markets: Mainly US customers, with offices and integration centres in Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B technology provider whose vendor partners sponsor F1; hospitality and technology showcase make it a plausible fit.

name: Aéma Groupe
desc: French mutual insurance group combining Macif, Aésio Mutuelle and Abeille Assurances, selling car, home, health and life cover.
markets: Customers mainly in France; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic French insurer with no international business; France hosts no Grand Prix today, so a weak F1 fit.
changed: Formed in 2021 by Macif and Aésio; bought Aviva France in 2021, renamed Abeille Assurances

name: S Group
desc: Finnish consumer co-operative group running Prisma and S-market supermarkets, hotels, restaurants, fuel stations and S-Bank.
markets: Mainly Finland, with Prisma stores in Estonia; left Russia in 2022.
rationale: Mainly Finnish retailer with small Estonian presence; little use for global F1 reach, a weak fit.

name: Inspire Brands
desc: Roark Capital-owned restaurant company owning Arby's, Buffalo Wild Wings, Sonic, Jimmy John's, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins.
markets: Mostly US restaurants; Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins franchises operate in many countries worldwide.
rationale: Mass-market US restaurant brands could use US races and fan promotions; plausible, as McDonald's partners exist in F1.

name: Royal London Group
desc: UK mutual insurer providing pensions, life insurance, protection and asset management.
markets: Customers in the United Kingdom and Ireland; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: UK-focused mutual; the British Grand Prix gives a local hook, but fit is weak.

name: Land O'Lakes, Inc.
desc: US agricultural co-operative making dairy foods and supplying animal feed, seed and crop protection products.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States; no verified wider international expansion.
rationale: Farm co-operative with a US grocery brand and US customers; little use for global F1 exposure, a weak fit.

name: Trader Joe's
desc: US grocery chain selling mostly own-label foods; owned by a trust of the Albrecht family behind Aldi Nord.
markets: Stores in the United States only; no international plans.
rationale: Does very little conventional advertising and sells only in the US; weak F1 fit.

name: Allegis Group
desc: Privately held staffing group providing recruitment and talent services through TEKsystems, Aerotek, Aston Carter and other brands.
markets: Clients across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through its staffing brands.
rationale: Rivals ManpowerGroup and Randstad already partner with F1; B2B hospitality could support client acquisition.

name: The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America
desc: US mutual insurer offering life, disability, dental and vision insurance to individuals and employers.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic US insurer with employer-benefits focus; US races are the only hook, so a weak fit.

name: American Family Insurance Group
desc: US mutual insurance group selling car, home, life and business insurance, also owning The General and Homesite.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic consumer insurer; US races give some exposure but fit is weak.

name: Kiewit Corporation
desc: Employee-owned construction and engineering firm building transportation, energy, water, industrial and building projects.
markets: Works mainly in the United States and Canada.
rationale: B2B contractor with no consumer brand and North American clients; weak F1 fit.

name: Farmers Insurance Exchange
desc: Policyholder-owned US reciprocal insurer selling car, home and business insurance, managed by Zurich-owned Farmers Group.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic consumer insurer with sports marketing experience; US races only, so fit is weak.
changed: Acquired MetLife's US property and casualty business in 2021

name: Decathlon
desc: Mulliez family-controlled sporting goods retailer that designs, makes and sells its own sports brands.
markets: Stores and online sales in dozens of countries across Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Americas and Africa.
rationale: Global sports brand reaching young families; F1 is plausible for brand building but not an obvious fit.

name: Mutual of Omaha Insurance Company
desc: US mutual insurer selling life, Medicare supplement, disability and other supplemental insurance plus banking.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic insurer with an older customer base and only US customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Copersucar S.A.
desc: Brazilian company owned by sugarcane mills that markets and trades their sugar and ethanol, including exports.
markets: Sells in Brazil and exports sugar worldwide; owns US ethanol marketer Eco-Energy.
rationale: B2B commodity trader with little consumer brand; São Paulo Grand Prix hospitality is the only hook, a weak fit.

name: Bloomberg L.P.
desc: Majority Michael Bloomberg-owned provider of financial data terminals, news, media, analytics and trading software.
markets: Customers and newsrooms in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Financial clients suit F1 hospitality, and data analytics offers a technology tie-in; rival Financial Times partners in F1.

name: McKinsey & Company
desc: Global management consulting partnership advising companies and governments on strategy, operations, technology and organisation.
markets: Offices in more than 60 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Rival consultancies partner with F1 teams; B2B hospitality and analytics showcase fit, though McKinsey markets conservatively.

name: The Whiting-Turner Contracting Company
desc: Employee-owned US construction manager and general contractor building commercial, healthcare, education and data-centre facilities.
markets: Works across the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B contractor with no consumer brand and US-only clients; weak F1 fit.

name: Hy-Vee, Inc.
desc: Employee-owned US supermarket chain with pharmacies and restaurants in several Midwestern states.
markets: Stores in the US Midwest only. Has sponsored IndyCar, so knows motorsport marketing.
rationale: Regional US grocer with IndyCar experience, but no Midwest F1 race; weak fit.
